sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized HA immunostaining in primary hippocampal neurons (L3). Receptor signaling function of the HA-tagged construct was NOT MEASURED explicitly; the ΔN variant (not the HA-tagged construct) was used for functional studies.
sites.rationale: Human ADGRA1 has no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–19 extracellular and TM1 beginning at residue 20, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus. The N-terminal HA tag on the mouse ortholog (L1–L5) therefore maps unambiguously to a prepend before human residue 1 (M), confirmed by Python: residue_after = seq[0] = 'M'. The 19-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample clearance from TM1 (>>3 residues). The mouse N-terminal sequence (MTQWDLKTVLSLPQYPGEFLHP, 22 aa) aligns closely with the human sequence (MDLKTVLSLPRYPGEFLHP, 19 aa), supporting transferability of the tagging strategy. Mouse ADGRA1 (UniProt Q8C4G9, close ortholog) was expressed as a full-length, membrane-anchored construct carrying an N-terminal HA tag in primary hippocampal neurons via lentivirus. Non-permeabilized immunostaining detected HA signal along MAP2-labeled dendrites and AnkG-labeled axon initial segments, confirming surface display of the tagged receptor. A ΔN variant replacing the first 22 mouse residues (MTQWDLKTVLSLPQYPGEFLHP) with 8×Gly was also described, establishing that the N-terminal extracellular region tolerates large substitutions without loss of surface trafficking.

sources.claim: Neurons sparsely receiving HA-ADGRA1 overexpression displayed surface HA signals along both MAP2-labeled dendrites and AnkG-labeled axon initial segments, suggesting subcellular localization to both pre- and postsynaptic sites ( Figure 2A ).

literature_notes: All five ledger clips (L1–L5) report the same experimental construct: N-terminally HA-tagged mouse ADGRA1 (Q8C4G9) expressed as a full-length, membrane-anchored receptor. L3 and L4/L5 confirm surface display by non-permeabilized staining. No internal extracellular loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or any other tag positions are reported in the ledger. The C-terminus of human ADGRA1 is intracellular (residues 306–560) and therefore does not qualify. The short extracellular loops ECL1 (75–84), ECL2 (156–175), and ECL3 (278–284) have no ledger-grounded insertion evidence and are not proposed. The ΔN variant (L1/L2) demonstrates that the N-terminal extracellular region is dispensable for surface trafficking, further supporting tolerance of an N-terminal tag, but it is not itself a tag-insertion site.
